feedback: You submitted a single PDF containing D4, your ethics stance, and on its own terms it is a strong, mature piece of work. You answer all four prompts in a clearly anchored first-person voice: you turn down the journalist's off-the-record DM and explain why off the record is a liability rather than a favour in a live incident, you define narrowly what you will and will not put in writing, you commit to presenting the decommissioning timeline factually to the security authority rather than handing it selectively to anyone who would use it as a shield or a weapon, and you name the action you take regardless of internal preference. You cite ISC2 Canon I and Canon II correctly by number and use Canon I well as the tiebreaker when obligations to the client and to the public pull apart. On the NDPA you correctly identify Sankofa as data controller, the duty to notify the regulator within the statutory window, and the duty to notify affected data subjects where the breach is high risk, anchored to the 312 customers and your own decode of the exfil. The one factual slip is that you name NITDA as the notifying authority when under the NDPA 2023 the supervisory authority is the NDPC; the obligations themselves are right, so this cost you only a small deduction rather than the row. Where I have to be honest with you is that this submission contained only D4. D1 the findings, D2 the exploit chain and CVSS, and D3 the written report were not present at your link, so each of those three deliverables scored zero, and that is why your overall number is low despite the quality of the ethics page. Nothing about the missing work reflects on the D4 you wrote; it simply was not there to grade. The single most important next step is to submit D1, D2, and D3, since those three carry 105 of the 120 marks and are the bulk of what this capstone is testing.

feedback: Adeoye, you submitted three of the four deliverables (D1 findings, D3 report, D4 ethics), and the work you did turn in shows real security instinct, so let me grade it fairly before naming what was missing. On D1 you wrote a clean, disciplined catalogue, but only two of the ten target vulnerabilities are actually present and properly evidenced: JWT alg:none (CWE-347, with the correct {"alg":"none"} header line) and XXE (CWE-611, with the file:///etc/passwd payload). Both of those are full-credit findings, and I gave you a little extra for correctly reasoning that the signature-pattern observation was a non-exploitable false positive rather than chasing it. The trouble is that the other four entries in your catalogue are really sub-aspects of those same two bugs, so the eight remaining key findings (SQL injection in login.php, unsalted MD5, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret, missing token expiry, the stored XSS beacon, path traversal, open redirect, and the missing cookie Secure/SameSite flags) simply are not there, which is why D1 lands at 7 of 30. D3 is your strongest piece: you ordered remediation by effort rather than by CVSS exactly as the brief asks, and you gave two genuine detection stopgaps with a data field and a false-positive rate each, which is precisely what was wanted. I docked D3 mainly because the business impact section is inflated and ungrounded, since you quoted 120,000 to 180,000 customers and billions of naira when the evidence shows 312 affected customers and tens of millions in balances. That is an overreach in framing rather than a faked artifact, so I did not apply a fabrication penalty, but please anchor impact to the actual exfil evidence next time. D4 reads in a confident, honest, first-person voice, you answered all four prompts, and you cited ISC2 canons by number, so that earned solid credit; it fell short of full marks only because the NDPA 2023 obligations stayed generic, with no section 40 (NDPC 72-hour notification) or section 41 (data-subject) citations. Now the part I have to state plainly and kindly: the D2 exploit chain and CVSS deliverable was not in your folder at all, so that entire 35-point section scored zero, and that single absence is the largest reason your total sits where it does. feedback: Enyi, you submitted three of the four deliverables (D1 findings, D3 report, D4 ethics), and I graded each of those on its own merits. Your D1 findings catalogue is the strongest part of the work: you cleanly nailed the SQL injection via string concatenation in the login query, the unsalted MD5 password hashing, the JWT alg:none acceptance, the unvalidated open redirect through the ?next parameter, and the session cookie missing its Secure flag, each with a real evidence line and a sensible OWASP and CWE pairing. Your D3 report shows you understood the business stakes, since the executive summary names the 312 affected customers, the roughly 10 million naira exposure, and the six-week BoltCash runway, but the two highest-weight parts of that deliverable, the effort-ordered remediation roadmap and the two detection stopgaps, were left as the bracketed template placeholders with no real fixes, no field or pattern names, and no false-positive estimates, so I could only credit the framing you actually wrote. Your D4 answered just one of the four ethics prompts and cited ISC2 canons 2 and 4 by number, which is good instinct, but it stopped short of the NDPA 2023 specifics (section 40 with the NDPC 72-hour clock and section 41 on data subjects) and the text carried OCR-style garbling that made it read as a rough draft. I want to be clear and fair about the gaps: D2, the exploit chain and CVSS scoring, was not in your folder at all, so it scored zero, and the unfinished placeholder portions of D3 and the three unanswered D4 prompts could not earn credit because there was nothing there to assess, not because I doubted you. None of this is a fabrication issue; the evidence you did cite lines up with the real artefacts, so there is no penalty, just unfinished work. The single most important next step is to build out the missing D2 exploit chain with the timestamped attacker timeline and a justified CVSS vector for the SQLi, since that deliverable is worth 35 points and is currently a clean zero that is fully recoverable.
